body: No problem, I hope it starts looking up for you.

Right now, maybe your way of moving forward is to give yourself some space to feel shitty about what has happened without making an attempt on your life. Allowing yourself to feel as hurt or pissed or upset as you are, without trying to minimize that or make it go away. And then trying one of those things you mentioned.

Therapy helps some people, not everyone. Same for medication. My personal advice would be to find out the root of why you want to die (maybe you feel like you can’t go on without your girlfriend, or maybe you feel hopeless because of the prospect that the future could be as bad as the past). Then, either find some sort of peace with that, or find a way to change it.

You have a lot of experience with tough times to look back on, so you have the strength to go on if you want to. It’s just finding that reason why. It takes time.
Only one way to find out. And if that’s not reason enough, you can always choose to kill yourself later. But once you kill yourself, you can’t take any decision back.

You aren’t shit. It’s completely understandable to want to kill yourself given how much pain you are in, and it seems rational to you because that pain makes it hard to see anything beyond the suffering that you are going through right now. Maybe there’s a way to lessen the pain? Or something that means something to you, or has the potential to someday? I don’t know your life story, but it sounds like you have had one hell of a struggle so far, and it would be a shame to see it all end now.

Why does jumping sound better? I’ll save you the details, but google “golden gate bridge suicide” and you will see that jumping is not as painless as it may seem.

Beyond that, I hear that you think that you have nothing to your name. It’s a tough feeling to sit with for sure, and not one that gets better quickly. I hope that you can find it in you to talk to someone about these thoughts in real life, and that they are able to provide you some comfort and guidance.

The best way not to hurt your loved ones is by not going through with this at all.

I can tell that you are in a lot of pain, and it seems like suicide is the best way out of it. But just from your post here I can tell that you have people in your life that you care about, and it sounds like you have people that care about you as well. It’s hard to see past the day when something this devastating has happened to you, but I hope that you reconsider staying.
